prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
ai_overview_text:
Several platforms and methods help check if ChatGPT and other AI engines recommend your small business. The best choice depends on your budget and whether you want a free check or ongoing tracking.
BaaDigi’s AI Search Visibility Tool: Best for local and service businesses. It runs a free, instant, geo-aware check across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overview for "near me" style prompts without requiring a signup. BaaDigi
Profound: A comprehensive AI marketing platform that tracks prompt volumes, brand visibility scores, competitor benchmarking, and citation analytics across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and more.
Frizerly: Specializes in Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) to help your business get cited and recommended by LLMs.
SE Ranking (AI Search Visibility Tracker): Good for small-to-midsize businesses that want AI tracking bundled alongside traditional SEO tools (tracking mentions across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and AI Overviews).
Ahrefs & Semrush: Both offer AI visibility-checking features to monitor brand mentions and cited pages across major AI models and search experiences. Profound +3
The Quick Manual Method (Free)
You can test your visibility right now directly inside the AI: Facebook·Brian Schreiner
Open ChatGPT (or Gemini, Perplexity, or Copilot).
Type a natural prompt your customers use, such as: "Who is the best [your service] in [your city]?"
See if your business name or a competitor comes up in the single-answer response. visibleowl.com +1
Why AI Chooses Businesses (and How to Get Recommended)
AI engines do not crawl your website the way traditional Google search does; instead, they weigh consensus from trusted third-party sources. AI models frequently pull recommendations and proof from platforms like: Instagram·Neil Patel +1
Reddit (top-ranked for trusted real-world user opinions)
YouTube (transcripts are indexed for proof of expertise)
Wikipedia (neutral background info)
LinkedIn and G2 (verified reviews and professional weight)
Consistent Google and Bing local listings with matching Name, Address, and Phone number (NAP) data. Facebook·Neil Patel +2
What type of small business you run (e.g., local contractor, e-commerce, local service)
What city or area you are located in
